claim_verdicts.evidence: --oneline: shorthand for "--pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit"; oneline = "<hash> <title-line>". git-commit: "The text up to the first blank line in a commit message is treated as the commit title". Lab run: a message whose line 2 is not blank was printed by --oneline with both lines joined. So --oneline prints the title, which equals the first line only when line 2 is blank.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `git log --oneline` prints one line per commit: the abbreviated commit id followed by the message's title — everything up to the first blank line, which is just the first line when a blank line follows it.
